ui.purpose: The engineered grotesque used for all UI chrome, labels, and body copy.

data.purpose: The data face. Every numeric, date, case-number, and currency value renders in this font with tabular figures — never the UI font.

page-title.purpose: One per page, top of the page-level heading.

body.purpose: The app's default text size — table cells, controls, body copy.

label.purpose: Table headers and fine print only; the sole size ever uppercased.

shadows.name: overlay
shadows.purpose: The only shadow role in the system: modals, popovers, and drawers exclusively. Panels at rest never carry a shadow.

shadows.name: overlay-dark
shadows.purpose: Dark-theme equivalent of the overlay shadow.

motion.name: ease-state
motion.purpose: Default timing for state changes: hover, expand, tab switch.

motion.name: ease-overlay
motion.purpose: Timing for overlays entering (modal, popover, drawer).

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The one filled button in the system; used for the single primary action in a form or panel.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { height: 30px; padding: 0 12px; border-radius: var(--r-ctl); border: 1px solid var(--primary); background: var(--primary); color: #fff; font-size: 13px; font-weight: 500; display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 6px; transition: background-color 120ms ease-out, border-color 120ms ease-out; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: var(--primary-strong); border-color: var(--primary-strong); }

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: The default button — white surface, hairline border; hover shifts to the primary color rather than filling the background.
components.css: .ds-btn-secondary { height: 30px; padding: 0 12px; border-radius: var(--r-ctl); border: 1px solid var(--border-strong); background: var(--surface); color: var(--text); font-size: 13px; font-weight: 500; transition: border-color 120ms ease-out, color 120ms ease-out; } .ds-btn-secondary:hover { border-color: var(--primary); color: var(--primary); }

components.name: Danger Button
components.description: Destructive actions. Color changes on hover, never layout — a destructive control should never visually jump.
components.css: .ds-btn-danger { height: 30px; padding: 0 12px; border-radius: var(--r-ctl); border: 1px solid var(--danger-border); background: var(--surface); color: var(--danger-text); font-size: 13px; font-weight: 500; transition: background-color 120ms ease-out, border-color 120ms ease-out; } .ds-btn-danger:hover { background: var(--danger-bg); border-color: var(--danger-text); }

components.name: Status Chip (Ok)
components.description: Dot-plus-text status indicator. Tone comes from a single status-to-tone map, never assigned ad hoc.
components.css: .ds-status { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 6px; height: 20px; padding: 0 8px; border-radius: var(--r-ctl); font-size: 12px; font-weight: 500; border: 1px solid; line-height: 1; } .ds-status-dot { width: 7px; height: 7px; border-radius: 50%; background: currentColor; } .ds-status-ok { color: var(--success-text); background: var(--success-bg); border-color: color-mix(in srgb, var(--success-text) 40%, transparent); }

components.name: Type Chip
components.description: Marks a work item's kind (deadline, task, event, service). Always uppercase, never a dot — visually distinct from a Status Chip on purpose.
components.css: .ds-typechip { display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: 0.04em; text-transform: uppercase; padding: 1px 6px; border-radius: var(--r-ctl); } .ds-typechip-deadline { color: var(--danger-text); background: var(--danger-bg); }

components.name: Metric Tile
components.description: Static display or, with a click handler, a toggleable filter facet — one component serves both.
components.css: .ds-tile { min-width: 0; height: 64px; padding: 10px 12px; background: var(--surface); border: 1px solid var(--border); border-radius: var(--r-panel); display: flex; flex-direction: column; justify-content: space-between; } .ds-tile-label { font-size: 11px; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.06em; color: var(--text-muted); font-weight: 600; } .ds-tile-value { font-family: var(--font-data); font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; font-size: 18px; font-weight: 500; line-height: 1; }

components.name: Panel
components.description: Flat at rest, hairline border, no shadow. The base container for nearly every surface in the app.
components.html:
Case Summary

Panel content goes here.
components.css: .ds-panel { background: var(--surface); border-radius: var(--r-panel); border: 1px solid var(--border); overflow: hidden; } .ds-panel-header { padding: 0.9rem 1.1rem; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--border); display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: space-between; } .ds-panel-header h3 { margin: 0; font-size: 15px; font-weight: 600; } .ds-panel-body { padding: 0.95rem 1.1rem 1.1rem; }

components.name: Filter Chip
components.description: Facet toggle inside the Filter Bar. On-state uses the same primary-soft/primary treatment as an active Metric Tile.
components.css: .ds-chip { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 6px; height: 24px; padding: 0 10px; border-radius: var(--r-ctl); border: 1px solid var(--border-strong); background: var(--surface); color: var(--text-muted); font-size: 12px; font-weight: 500; transition: border-color 120ms ease-out, background-color 120ms ease-out, color 120ms ease-out; } .ds-chip-on { background: var(--primary-soft); border-color: var(--primary); color: var(--primary); } .ds-chip-count { color: var(--warning-text); font-weight: 600; }

components.name: Empty State
components.description: Left-aligned title, optional muted hint, optional action. Has a dedicated table-row mode so an empty table never needs a hand-built row.
components.html:
No matching cases

Try clearing a filter.
components.css: .ds-empty { display: grid; gap: 6px; justify-items: start; padding: 24px 16px; text-align: left; } .ds-empty-title { margin: 0; font-weight: 500; color: var(--text); } .ds-empty-hint { margin: 0; font-size: 12px; color: var(--text-muted); }

narrative.overview: A state-agency litigation tool should feel like a precisely engineered public document: calm, exact, authoritative, zero decoration. The voice comes from three deliberate choices working together — an engineered grotesque paired with a monospaced data face, a disciplined cool-neutral surface system, and exactly one confident accent blue. Arkansas crimson appears exactly once in the entire system, as the brand tick in the app bar; it is never reused as a semantic or decorative color anywhere else. This identity was chosen over a "Brief" legal-paper direction (Source Serif display, warm neutrals, oxblood accent) specifically because the daily surface is dense tables that attorneys scan all day: the warm/serif direction softened data contrast, complicated dark mode, and traded scanability for atmosphere. It was also chosen over a slate-and-signal-orange "ops console" direction, rejected because it read as SRE tooling rather than counsel, and its orange collided with the warning color in a deadline-heavy interface.
keyCharacteristics: One accent color carries every action and active state; nothing else competes with it.
Status is never color-only — a dot plus text label together carry every state.
Panels are flat with a single hairline border; elevation is a last resort, reserved for true overlays.
Every numeric, date, case-number, or currency value renders in the monospaced data face with tabular figures.
Sixteen selectable themes share one semantic contract, so which theme is active never changes what a color communicates.

rules.name: The One Tick Rule
rules.body: Arkansas Crimson appears in exactly one place: the brand tick in the app bar. It is never a status color, never a hover state, never reused for emphasis.

rules.name: The Dot-Plus-Text Rule
rules.body: Status is never carried by color alone. Every status chip pairs a colored dot with a text label; every chart uses direct labels rather than a color-only legend.

rules.name: The Tabular Everything Rule
rules.body: Every numeric, date, case-number, and currency value in a table cell or metric tile renders in the data font with tabular-nums — no exceptions.

rules.name: The No-Italics Rule
rules.body: UI chrome never uses italics. No 700-weight type exists anywhere in the system — 600 is the ceiling.

rules.name: The Flat-at-Rest Rule
rules.body: A panel earns a shadow only by becoming an overlay (modal, popover, drawer). A panel in the normal page flow is always flat with a border, never a shadow.

dos: Do keep Docket Blue as the only accent color competing for attention on any screen.
Do pair every status indicator with a text label; color alone never carries a state.
Do render every number, date, case number, and currency value in the data font with tabular figures.
Do keep panels flat (border only) at rest; reserve the overlay shadow for modals, popovers, and drawers.
Do treat all sixteen themes as re-skins of one semantic contract.
Do use full month names with no ordinal for dates, always suffixed with CT for date-times.
Do render an unset value as an em dash in muted text rather than a repeated string like "Not set".
donts: Don't reuse Arkansas Crimson anywhere except the app-bar brand tick.
Don't introduce a new radius value outside 4px (controls) / 8px (panels) / 999px (circular).
Don't use italics anywhere in UI chrome, or any font weight heavier than 600.
Don't add decorative animation; motion is functional-only and disabled under prefers-reduced-motion.
Don't revive the rejected "Brief" (legal-paper) or "Control" (ops-console) directions.
